verses.zh: 我观看，见基路伯头上的穹苍之中，显出蓝宝石的形状，彷佛宝座的形像。
verses.en: As I watched, I saw[NOTE:1] on the platform[NOTE:2] above the top of the cherubim something like a sapphire, resembling the shape of a throne, appearing above them.
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.
Or “like a dome.” See 1:22-26.

verses.zh: 主对那穿细麻衣的人说：「你进去，在旋转的轮内基路伯以下，从基路伯中间将火炭取满两手，撒在城上。」我就见他进去。
verses.en: The Lord[NOTE:1] said to the man dressed in linen, “Go between the wheelwork[NOTE:2] underneath the cherubim.[NOTE:3] Fill your hands with burning coals from among the cherubim and scatter them over the city.” He went as I watched.
notes: Heb “and he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The Hebrew term often refers to chariot wheels (Isa 28:28; Ezek 23:24; 26:10).

The LXX, Syriac, Vulgate, and Targum mss read plural “cherubim,” while the MT is singular here, “cherub.” The plural ending was probably omitted in copying the MT due to the similar beginning of the next word.

verses.zh: 那人进去的时候，基路伯站在殿的右边，云彩充满了内院。
verses.en: (The cherubim were standing on the south side[NOTE:1] of the temple when the man went in, and a cloud filled the inner court.)
notes: Heb “right side.”

verses.zh: 耶和华的荣耀从基路伯那里上升，停在门槛以上；殿内满了云彩，院宇也被耶和华荣耀的光辉充满。
verses.en: Then the glory of the Lord arose from the cherub and moved to the threshold of the temple. The temple was filled with the cloud while the court was filled with the brightness of the Lord’s glory.

verses.zh: 基路伯翅膀的响声听到外院，好像全能　神说话的声音。
verses.en: The sound of the wings of the cherubim could be heard from the outer court, like the sound of the Sovereign God[NOTE:1] when he speaks.
notes: The name (“El Shaddai”) has often been translated “God Almighty,” primarily because Jerome translated it omnipotens (“all powerful”) in the Latin Vulgate. There has been much debate over the meaning of the name. For discussion see W. F. Albright, “The Names Shaddai and Abram,” JBL 54 (1935): 173-210; R. Gordis, “The Biblical Root sdy-sd,” JTS 41 (1940): 34-43; and especially T. N. D. Mettinger, In Search of God, 69-72.

verses.zh: 他吩咐那穿细麻衣的人说：「要从旋转的轮内基路伯中间取火。」那人就进去站在一个轮子旁边。
verses.en: When the Lord[NOTE:1] commanded the man dressed in linen, “Take fire from within the wheelwork, from among the cherubim,” the man[NOTE:2] went in and stood by one of the wheels.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “he”; the referent (the man dressed in linen) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “the wheel.”

verses.zh: 有一个基路伯从基路伯中伸手到基路伯中间的火那里，取些放在那穿细麻衣的人两手中，那人就拿出去了。
verses.en: Then one of the cherubim[NOTE:1] stretched out his hand[NOTE:2] toward the fire that was among the cherubim. He took some and put it into the hands of the man dressed in linen, who took it and left.
notes: Heb “the cherub.”
The Hebrew text adds, “from among the cherubim.”

verses.zh: 在基路伯翅膀之下，显出有人手的样式。
verses.en: (The cherubim appeared to have the form[NOTE:1] of human hands under their wings.)
notes: The Hebrew term is normally used as an architectural term in describing the plan or pattern of the tabernacle or temple or a representation of it (see Exod 25:8; 1 Chr 28:11).

verses.zh: 我又观看，见基路伯旁边有四个轮子。这基路伯旁有一个轮子，那基路伯旁有一个轮子，每基路伯都是如此；轮子的颜色（原文是形状）彷佛水苍玉。
verses.en: As I watched, I noticed[NOTE:1] four wheels by the cherubim, one wheel beside each cherub;[NOTE:2] the wheels gleamed like jasper.[NOTE:3]
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.
The MT repeats this phrase either due to dittography or a distributive meaning of the repeated phrase (see GKC, 134q).
Heb “Tarshish stone.” The meaning is uncertain. The term has also been translated “topaz” (NEB, NIV11), “beryl” (KJV, NASB, NRSV), and “chrysolite” (RSV, NIV84).

verses.zh: 至于四轮的形状，都是一个样式，彷佛轮中套轮。
verses.en: As for their appearance, all four of them looked the same, something like a wheel within a wheel.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “like a wheel at right angles to another wheel.” Some envision concentric wheels here, while others propose “a globe-like structure in which two wheels stand at right angles” (L. C. Allen, Ezekiel [WBC], 1:33-34). See also 1:16.

verses.zh: 轮行走的时候，向四方都能直行，并不掉转。头向何方，他们也随向何方，行走的时候并不掉转。
verses.en: When they[NOTE:1] moved, they would go in any of the four directions they faced without turning as they moved; in the direction the head would turn they would follow[NOTE:2] without turning as they moved,
notes: That is, the cherubim.
Many interpreters assume that the human face of each cherub was the one that looked forward.

verses.zh: 他们全身，连背带手和翅膀，并轮周围都满了眼睛。这四个基路伯的轮子都是如此。
verses.en: along with their entire bodies,[NOTE:1] their backs, their hands, and their wings. The wheels of the four of them were full of eyes all around.
notes: The phrase “along with their entire bodies” is absent from the LXX and may be a gloss explaining the following words.

verses.zh: 至于这些轮子，我耳中听见说是旋转的。
verses.en: As for their wheels, they were called “the wheelwork”[NOTE:1] as I listened.
notes: Or “the whirling wheels.”

verses.zh: 基路伯各有四脸：第一是基路伯的脸，第二是人的脸，第三是狮子的脸，第四是鹰的脸。
verses.en: Each of the cherubim[NOTE:1] had four faces: The first was the face of a cherub,[NOTE:2] the second that of a man, the third that of a lion, and the fourth that of an eagle.
notes: Heb “each one”; the referent (the cherubim) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

The living creature described here is thus slightly different from the one described in Ezek 1:10, where an ox’s face appeared instead of a cherub’s. Note that some English versions harmonize the two descriptions and read the same here as in 1:10 (cf. NAB, NLT “an ox”; TEV, CEV “a bull”). This may be justified based on v. 22, which states the creatures’ appearance was the same.

verses.zh: 基路伯升上去了；这是我在迦巴鲁河边所见的活物。
verses.en: The cherubim rose up; these were the living beings[NOTE:1] I saw at the Kebar River.
notes: Heb “it was the living creature.”

verses.zh: 基路伯行走，轮也在旁边行走。基路伯展开翅膀，离地上升，轮也不转离他们旁边。
verses.en: When the cherubim moved, the wheels moved beside them; when the cherubim spread[NOTE:1] their wings to rise from the ground, the wheels did not move from their side.
notes: Heb “lifted.”

verses.zh: 那些站住，这些也站住；那些上升，这些也一同上升，因为活物的灵在轮中。
verses.en: When the cherubim[NOTE:1] stood still, the wheels[NOTE:2] stood still, and when they rose up, the wheels[NOTE:3] rose up with them, for the spirit[NOTE:4] of the living beings[NOTE:5] was in the wheels.[NOTE:6]
notes: Heb “they”; the referent (the cherubim) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “they”; the referent (the wheels) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “they”; the referent (the wheels) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Or “wind.”
Heb “living creature.”
Heb “them”; the referent (the wheels) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 耶和华的荣耀从殿的门槛那里出去，停在基路伯以上。
verses.en: Then the glory of the Lord moved away from the threshold of the temple and stopped above the cherubim.

verses.zh: 基路伯出去的时候，就展开翅膀，在我眼前离地上升。轮也在他们的旁边，都停在耶和华殿的东门口。在他们以上有以色列　神的荣耀。
verses.en: The cherubim spread[NOTE:1] their wings, and they rose up from the earth[NOTE:2] while I watched (when they went, the wheels went alongside them). They stopped at the entrance to the east gate of the Lord’s temple as the glory of the God of Israel hovered above them.
notes: Heb “lifted.”
Or “the ground” (NIV, NCV).

verses.zh: 这是我在迦巴鲁河边所见、以色列　神荣耀以下的活物，我就知道他们是基路伯。
verses.en: These were the living creatures[NOTE:1] that I saw at the Kebar River underneath the God of Israel; I knew that they were cherubim.
notes: Heb “That was the living creature.”

verses.zh: 各有四个脸面，四个翅膀，翅膀以下有人手的样式。
verses.en: Each had four faces; each had four wings and the form of human hands under the wings.

verses.zh: 至于他们脸的模样，并身体的形像，是我从前在迦巴鲁河边所看见的。他们俱各直往前行。
verses.en: As for the form of their faces, they were the faces whose appearance I had seen at the Kebar River. Each one moved straight ahead.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing
is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 10:1-2

1Then I looked, and behold, in the expanse that was over the heads of the cherubim something
like a sapphire stone, in appearance resembling a throne, appeared above them. 2And He spoke to the man clothed in linen and said, "Enter between
the whirling wheels under the cherubim and fill your hands with coals of fire from between the cherubim and scatter them over the city." And he entered in my sight.

10:1-2 This is YHWH's portable throne chariot of Ezek. 1:13-25. It will return to the temple in Ezek. 43:1-9.

10:1 "the expanse" See note at Ezek. 1:22.

▣

NASB, NKJV, LXX, JPSOA
"like a sapphire stone"

NRSV
"like a sapphire"

TEV
"a throne made of sapphire"

REB
"a sapphire in the shape

of a throne"

NJB
"something like sapphire"

Peshitta
"something with the appearance

of a sapphire stone"

The MT has a NOUN CONSTRUCT (BDB 6 "stone" and BDB 705 "sapphire) in Ezek. 10:1.
This jewel appears several times.

- a pavement under YHWH's feet at Mt. Sinai ‒ Exod. 24:10

- a jewel in the ephod of the High Priest ‒ Exod. 28:18; 39:11

- foundation of the restored people of God to the Promised Land ‒ Isa. 54:11

- YHWH's throne in the midst of His portable throne chariot ‒ Ezek. 1:26; 10:1

- the covering of a cherub in Eden, used as imagery of the King of Tyre ‒ Ezek. 28:13

This jewel's name comes into Hebrew as a loan word from Sanskrit. It is a bluish (i.e. the color of the sky), brittle composite
stone from Afghanistan. In Akkadian texts, it is mentioned as part of the temple structure dedicated to "the high god."

Since Pliny it has been identified as lapis lazuli (i.e. Persian loan word).

10:2 YHWH gives three commands to the angelic being dressed in linen.

- "enter," BDB 97, KB 112, Qal IMPERATIVE

- "fill," BDB 569, KB 583, Piel IMPERATIVE

- "scatter," BDB 284, KB 283, Qal IMPERATIVE

The imagery comes from the vision of Isa. 6:6, where it is initially a purification ritual
inaugurating Isaiah's ministry. Here it is a judgment ritual, which is repeated in Rev. 8:5. In may ways
Isaiah (i.e. chapter 24) and Ezekiel are an initial example of apocalyptic imagery. This is developed in
Daniel and Zechariah and becomes a significant Jewish genre during the interbiblical period.

SPECIAL TOPIC: APOCALYPTIC LITERATURE

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 10:3-5

3Now the cherubim were standing on the right side of the temple when the man entered, and the cloud filled the inner court. 4Then the glory of the Lord went up from the cherub to the threshold of the temple, and the temple was filled with the cloud and the court was filled with the brightness of the glory of the Lord. 5Moreover, the sound of the wings of the cherubim was heard as far as the outer court, like the voice of God Almighty when He speaks.

10:3 "the cloud filled the inner court" This is the theophanic cloud (BDB 777) of glory (a visual symbol
of the presence of YHWH) that was present

- at the crossing of the Red Sea (cf. Exod. 13:21)

- on Mount Sinai (cf. Exod. 24:14-18)

- at the tabernacle of Moses (cf. Exod. 40:34-38; Num. 14:14)

- at the dedication of Solomon's temple (cf. 1 Kgs. 8:11; 2 Chr. 5:13-14)

- in Isaiah's vision (cf. Isa. 6:4)

- in Ezekiel's vision (cf. Ezek. 1:4)

- at the baptism of Jesus (cf. Mark 1:10-11)

- at the transfiguration of Jesus (cf. Matt. 17:5)

- at the ascension of Jesus (Acts 1:9)

- at the return of Jesus (cf. Matt. 24:30; 26:64; Mark 14:62; Luke 21:27; 1 Thess. 4:17; Rev. 1:7)

This ADJECTIVE "inner" (BDB 819) refers to parts of the temple or a
king's palace (cf. Esther 4:11; 5:1). The VERB form means "to turn a specific
direction" (cf. Ezek. 8:3). Ezekiel uses this term twenty-four times in his discussions of the Jerusalem
temple and his eschatological temple.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH

10:4 "the glory of the Lord. . .brightness of the glory of the Lord"
Brightness becomes an added characteristic of His glory (cf. Ezek. 1:4,28) during the Wilderness Wandering
period (i.e. the Shekinah Cloud of Glory).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (kabod, OT)

▣ "the threshold" See full note at Ezek. 9:3.

10:5 "the sound of the wings of the Cherubim" For the full notes see Ezek. 1:24.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHERUBIM

▣ "God Almighty" This is the Hebrew title El Shaddai. This was the Patriarchal name for
Israel's Deity (cf. Exod. 6:3). It is first used as a self-designation by YHWH to Abram in Gen. 17:6.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ALMIGHTY (Shaddai)

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 10:6-8

6It came about when He commanded the man clothed in linen, saying, "Take fire
from between the whirling wheels, from between the cherubim," he entered and stood beside a wheel. 7Then the cherub stretched
out his hand from between the cherubim to the fire which was between the cherubim, took some and put it into the hands of the one clothed
in linen, who took it and went out. 8The cherubim appeared to have the form of a man's hand under their wings.

10:6 "Take fire from between the whirling wheels and from between the Cherubim" The
VERB (BDB 542, KB 534, Qal IMPERATIVE)
is the fourth command to this angelic being (i.e. "the man clothed in linen," cf. Ezek. 10:2). This is obviously a reference to the burning
coals, which represent God's holiness (i.e. Isa. 6:6).

10:7-8, 11-12, 14 The full description of the Cherubim is given in Ezek. 1:5-14.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHERUBIM

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 10:9-14

9Then I looked, and behold, four wheels beside the cherubim, one wheel beside
each cherub; and the appearance of the wheels was like the gleam of a Tarshish stone. 10As for their appearance, all four of
them had the same likeness, as if one wheel were within another wheel. 11When they moved, they went in any of their four directions
without turning as they went; but they followed in the direction which they faced, without turning as they went. 12Their whole body, their backs,
their hands, their wings, and the wheels were full of eyes all around, the wheels belonging to all four of them. 13The wheels were called in my
hearing, the whirling wheels. 14And each one had four faces. The first face was the face of a cherub, the second face was the
face of a man, the third the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle.

10:9-10, 13 The full description of the wheels is found in Ezek. 1:15-21.

10:9 "a Tarshish stone" See SPECIAL TOPIC: TARSHISH

10:12 "Their whole body, their back, and their hands, and their wings, and the wheels were full of eyes
all around" This is an expansion of the description found in chapter 1, where the eyes were only found on
the wheels (cf. Ezek. 1:18; Rev. 4:6,8). It seems to be an intensification of the all-knowingness of God.
This is in contrast to the statements of the idolaters in Ezek. 8:12 and which is reacted to by God in
Ezek. 9:9.

10:14 "The first face was the face of a cherub" In Ezek. 1:10 it was the face of an ox.
There is no real explanation for the change (cf. Rev. 4:7). Even in the book of Ezekiel it seems that
the description changes even again in Ezek. 41:18-19.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 10:15-17

15Then the cherubim rose up. They are the living beings that I saw by the river Chebar.
16Now when the cherubim moved, the wheels would go beside them; also when the cherubim lifted up their wings to rise from the ground,
the wheels would not turn from beside them. 17When the cherubim stood still, the wheels would stand still; and when they rose up, the wheels
would rise with them, for the spirit of the living beings was in them.

10:15, 20 "The cherubim rose up. They are the living beings that I saw at the river Chebar" Possibly,
Ezekiel had not been in the inner court of the temple. Although he was in training to become a priest
he was exiled before his thirtieth year. Apparently when he saw the pictures on the inside of the temple
he recognized the creatures he saw in chapter 1 were the Cherubim.

10:17

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA
"for the spirit of the living being

was in them"

TEV
"because the creatures controlled

them"

NJB
"since they shared the same living

spirit"

LXX, Peshitta
"because the spirit of life was

in them"

Rotherham
"for the spirit of the living one was

in them"

The inanimate wheels followed the will of the four living creatures that supported the throne. The throne moved at YHWH's direction.
It could move on the ground (i.e. wheels) and through the air (cherubim wings) in any direction.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 10:18-19

18Then the glory of the Lord departed from the threshold
of the temple and stood over the cherubim. 19When the cherubim departed, they lifted their wings and rose up from the earth in my sight
with the wheels beside them; and they stood still at the entrance of the east gate of the Lord's house, and the glory of the
God of Israel hovered over them.

10:18 God returns to His throne chariot. This is anthropomorphic imagery.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE DEITY

10:19 This is the initial sequence of YHWH leaving His temple. This is where the symbolic title "Ichabod,"
which means "the glory has departed" (BDB 33, cf. 1 Sam. 4:21), was put over the temple. It is one thing
for YHWH to refuse to listen to His people. It is far more devastating that He leave His temple!

The rabbis speculate that God stayed three and a half years on the Mount of Olives (cf. Ezek. 11:22-23) hoping that the
Jews would repent, but they would not. This is surely an exaggeration. So He moved east to be with the exiles who formed a nucleus of the
people of God who would return. The glory returns to this temple in Ezek. 43:12.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 10:20-22

20These are the living beings that I saw beneath the God of Israel
by the river Chebar; so I knew that they were cherubim. 21Each one had four faces and each one four wings, and beneath their wings
was the form of human hands. 22As for the likeness of their faces, they were the same faces whose appearance I had seen by the river
Chebar. Each one went straight ahead.

10:20 "cherubim" See SPECIAL TOPIC: CHERUBIM
